1. Plaint
 1.1.

Plaintiff has filed the present suit claiming to be the owner of  Property bearing No.898-900, Gali To  Novelty Cinema, S.P. Mukherji Marg, Delhi-110006, on the  grounds that the Defendants who are in occupation of portion  of the first floor and second floor of the said property as  tenants for residential purposes alone, are using the said  premises for storing heavy motor truck tyres, tubes, rims and  other accessories related to the business of motor and truck  tyres, tubes and rims etc, being run by them under the name CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. 
 of M/s Rajasthan Trading Company, at 882 behind Novelty  Cinema, S.P. Mukherji Marg, Delhi-110006.
That the labours  of the Defendants are also living and cooking in the said  premises, because of which the walls and rooms of the  premises have developed cracks and are getting damaged.

Because of the aforesaid cooking by labours of the  defendants in a place where tyres, tubes etc are being stored,
 there is also chance of fire in the building.

1.2. Accordingly, the Plaintiff has claimed damages @ Rs.10,000/-
 per month for the three years preceding to the filing of the suit  i.e. total Rs.3,60,000/- and Plaintiff has also prayed for  Mandatory Injunction so as to direct the Defendants to remove  all the stored tyres, tubes etc from the tenanted premises and Ved Prakash vs Vijay Laxmi on 2 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59662408/
1  also to stop labours from using the said premises from living  and cooking.
2. WRITTEN STATEMENT  2.1.

In the Written Statement, the Defendants admitted that they  were paying rent to the Plaintiff and submitted that the  property was let out by Sh.Raghunath Prasad in the year  1971 to the Father-in-law of Defendant No.1 and Grand-  Father of Defendant No.2 to 4.

They submitted that the  premises was let out for residential-cum-commercial purposes  and alleged that the rent receipts on which the Plaintiff has  relied upon to prove the nature of tenancy is manipulated.

As  regards, storage of tyres, tubes, rims in the tenanted  premises, the Defendants submitted that the tenanted  premises was occupied by the Defendants as well as by their CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. 
 servants to look after the goods stored there, as the tenanted  premises was taken on rent for the purpose of storing the  tyres and other goods as well as for the residence of the  Defendants.

They denied that the property has got  damaged because of storage of articles by the Defendants.

They submitted that the Plaintiff himself is using the remaining  portion of the building for storing heavy cartoons and heavy  bags of medicines etc and he is neither carrying out repairs  nor permitting the Defendant to carry out repairs in the said  property.
Lastly, they prayed for dismissal of the suit.
3. In Replication to the Written Statement, the Plaintiff has denied  the averments made by the Defendant and reiterated the  contents of the Plaint.

4. After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed in  the present case on 20.03.2013 :-
 a) Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the recovery of  Rs.3,60,000/- as prayed for?
OPP  b) Whether plaintiff is entitled for interest, if so at what rate  and for what period?
OPP  c) Whether the suit is not properly valued for the purposes of  court fees and jurisdiction?

OPD  e) Whether plaintiff has not come to the court with clean CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. 
 hands and suppressed material facts?

OPD  5.1.
The onus to prove the said issue is upon the Defendant and Ved Prakash vs Vijay Laxmi on 2 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59662408/

2  the said issue has arisen in view of Para-1 of Preliminary  Objections in Written Statement, which is reproduced as  under:-
 "That the present suit is not properly valued for the  purposes of court fee and jurisdiction and the plaintiff has  not paid / affixed required court fee with the plaint.
Hence  the present suit is not maintainable."

5.2. It is not clarified in the aforesaid paragraph as to how the suit  is not properly valued for the purpose of court fees and  jurisdiction and even in the Written Submissions filed by the  Defendants on 05.04.2017, it is not mentioned as to how the  suit has not been properly valued and that what should have  been the value of the suit for the purpose of court fees and  jurisdiction as per the Defendants.

5.3 . At this stage, the court would like to reproduce Para-12 of the  Plaint as under :-
 "That value of the suit for purpose of jurisdiction and court  fees is Rs.3,60,130/- as detailed below on which advalorem  court fee of Rs.5,990/- has been paid:
 a) Claim of damages for three Value Court fee  years @ Rs.10,000/- p.m. 3,60,000/- 5,990/-

a) Relief of Mandatory injunction 130/-

 5.4.

sentences.text:
As per the aforesaid paragraph, the Plaintiff has valued the  suit for purpose of damages @ Rs.3,60,000/- and for the relief  of Mandatory Injunction @ Rs.130/-.
 5.5.
As per Section-7(i) of Court Fees Act, 1917, the amount of the  fee payable in a suit for money, including suit for damages  and compensation, shall be computed according to the  amount claimed.

In the present case, the Plaintiff has claimed  damages of Rs.3,60,000/- and has valued the suit @
 Rs.3,60,000/- for the said damages, therefore, the suit is  correctly valued by the Plaintiff for the relief of damages.

5.6. As far as relief of Mandatory Injunction is concerned, as per Section-7(iv)(d) of the Court Fees Act r/w Punjab Amendment  Act 26 of 1949, the value of such suit for the purpose of Court  Fees is ad valorem on the amount of relief sought as valued  and stated in the Plaint by the Plaintiff, provided that minimum  court fees of Rs.13/- has to be paid.

In the present case, the  Plaintiff has valued the relief of Mandatory Injunction @
 Rs.130/- and has paid the minimum court fees of Rs.13/- upon  the same.
5.7 . In the opinion of the court, the suit is properly valued and  court fees has been paid accordingly,
Hence, this issue is  decided in favour of the Plaintiff and against the Defendants.
6. Issue No.4: Whether the jurisdiction of this court is barred  under the provisions of Delhi Rent Control Act ? OPD  6.1.

, the plaintiff has filed two eviction  petitions and the present suit.
The eviction petitions were  dismissed by the learned ARC and appeal against the  same is pending.

So the jurisdiction of this Hon'ble court is  barred under the provisions of Delhi Rent Control Act."
 6.2.

As per Section-50 of Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, a civil court  shall not entertain any suit or proceeding in so far as it relates  to the fixation of standard rent in relation to any premises to  which the Act applies or to eviction of any tenant therefrom or  to any other matter which the Controller is empowered by or  under the Act to decide and no Injunction in respect of any  action taken or to be taken by the Controller under the said  Act shall be granted by any civil court.

In the present suit, the  Plaintiff has sought damages from the Defendants for causing  damages to the tenanted premises and there is no provision  under Delhi Rent Control Act, under which damages can be  awarded by the Controller to the landlord for the damages  caused to the tenanted premises by the Tenant.

Further,
 though Section-14(c) of Delhi Rent Control Act provides that  the use of the tenanted premises for a purpose other than that  for which the same has been let, is a ground for eviction of the  tenant from the tenanted premises, but there is no provision in  the said Act by which the Controller can issue Injunction to the  Tenant to not to use the said tenanted premises in a particular  manner, therefore, the present suit is not hit by Section-50 of  Delhi Rent Control Act and this issue is decided in favour of CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. 
 the Plaintiff and against the Defendant.

damaged and cracks have appeared therein.

In order to claim damages, the Plaintiff is required to prove the  following facts :-
 a) That damage is caused to the building / tenanted  premises.
 b) That such damage is not normal wear and tear but caused  due to the conduct of Defendants of storing tyres, tubes etc  in the tenanted premises.
 c) That the approximate cost of repair of the said damage is  Rs.3,60,000/-.
 7.6.
The very first fact that the Plaintiff was required to prove, was  that actual damage was caused to building / tenanted  premises, beyond normal wear and tear.

7.7. To prove the said fact, Plaintiff testified as PW-1 and in his  Affidavit he reproduced the contents of Plaint and stated in  Para-8 as under :-
 "Defendants started using the tenanted premises on the  first and second floor let for residence only for storing  heavy motor trucks tyres, tubes, rims and other  accessories in bulk and keep the portion packed to the  maximum of their capacity and as a consequence thereof  the walls, floors, roofs of the tenanted premises have gone  damaged by appearing cracks therein and are getting  damaged for their day to day ..............
The damage cause  to the property has been seen by the Deponent with his  own eyes".

7.8. The Plaintiff could not be cross-examined as he expired  before he could be cross-examined, but even if his testimony  is taken to be true, still the same is bereft of the description of  damage, kind of damage, extent / nature of damage that has CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs.  been caused to the building.

5  valuation report."
7.11. He also admitted "We did not file any complaint before any  authority for damage caused to suit property by defendant".

7.12. Thus, this witness admitted that there was no basis for  claiming damage @ Rs.10,000/- per month for any damage  caused to building and like PW-1 he also failed to prove the  kind / nature of damage that the suit property suffered due to  storage of alleged articles by the Defendants.
 7.13. PW-3
Ved Prakash Kasana has tendered his Affidavit as  Ex.PW3/A.

In his affidavit he has not mentioned about any  damage to the suit property but in last Para of Affidavit (i.e.
 Para-5) he testified as under :-
 "That, whenever the deponent visited the suit property, the  deponent found the family of the defendants residing  therein and no commercial activity or storage of tyres etc in CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors.

As this witness did not testify regarding damage to building in  his affidavit, hence there is no question to said witness in this  regard.

7.15. Last witness examined by plaintiff is PW-4 Sh. Shashi Sareen,
 who in his affidavit Ex. PW 4/A deposed that huge cracks  have developed in the walls, floors and the floors of the rooms  are sinking.

He also testified that the plaintiffs have stored  tyres, tubes and rims etc. in the suit premises and that labour  of the defendants are living in the tenanted premises and also  cooking food there.
 7.16.
In his cross examination this witness stated that the plaintiff
has shop at ground floor of the building and that he stores his  goods on the floors above and that workers of the plaintiff as  well as defendants are residing in the building.

Though, the testimony of this witness regarding damage to  property i.e. "big cracks" in the walls and floors remained  unchallenged, because there is no cross examination in this  regard, however, his unchallenged testimony in this regard  also does not prove the fact that the said cracks have  developed because of storage of tyers etc. by the defendant  or because of the fact that the building is very old or for the  reason that the plaintiff is also storing the goods on the upper CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors. 
 floors of the building.

Moreover, his testimony is of no help to  prove the fact that the damage caused to the suit property  can be repaired and that such repair would entail cost of  Rs.10,000/- per month or Rs.3,60,000/- in total.

In defence evidence, defendant No.2 Chetan Gupta testified  as DW-1 and in his affidavit Ex. DW 1/A, he testified that the  present suit has been filed by plaintiff only to pressurize the Ved Prakash vs Vijay Laxmi on 2 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59662408/

That eviction petition  filed by plaintiff were dismissed by Ld. affidavit the witness stated that the tenanted premises is  occupied by defendants as well as by their servants, who look  after the goods stored there, as the tenanted premises was  taken on rent for purpose of storing tyres and other goods as  well as for residence of defendants.

As regards injunction it may be noted that the plaintiff had also  filed an eviction petition under Section 14 (1) (c) of Delhi Rent  Control Act on 26.03.2010, in which it was pleaded that the  tenanted premises was let out for residential purposes and the  defendant was misusing the same for commercial purposes  by storing tyres therein without the consent of the plaintiff.

sentences.text: Page No. 12 of 15 tenanted premises since long.
It is averred by the petitioners that the tenanted premises is being used by the respondents for commercial purposes, i.e., for storage of tyres etc. and that same is lying locked for several years.
The case of the petitioners is that the tenanted premises was let out solely for residential purpose.
However, no document has been filed by the petitioners to substantiate that the tenanted premises was let out solely for residential purposes.

On the other hand, the respondents have averred that the tenanted premises was let out for composite purpose and the respondents are using some portions of the tenanted premises for commercial purposes and remaining portion for residential purposes for themselves and their servants.

The respondents in order to prove their residence over the tenanted premises have filed the photocopy of passbook of respondent No.1 where the address of respondent No.1 is shown to be of the tenanted premises.

Copy of income tax return, Election ID card, LIC renewal receipt, bank letters as well as the other insurance premium receipts have also been filed which go on to prove that in all these documents,
the respondents have mentioned their address to be of the tenanted premises.

These documents clearly prove that the tenanted premises is being used for residential purposes by the respondents and that the contention of the petitioner that none of the respondents is residing at the tenanted premises does not hold any ground.
The petitioners have also sought to prove that the tenanted premises was let out solely for residential purposes by virtue of rent receipt wherein the word "RIHAISH" has been mentioned.
On the other hand, the case of the respondents is that the said word "RIHAISH" has been added by the petitioners subsequently and that in the original rent receipts there is no said word "RIHAISH".
From perusal of the said rent receipts, it is clear that the said word has been added subsequently since it is not in proper column where it should have been stated.
No other document has been filed by the petitioners to show that the tenanted premises was let out solely for residential purposes.

The respondents have also filed copy of the electricity bill for the year 2011, 2012, 2013 and 2014 in order to prove that the respondents are residing in the t e n a n t e d p r e m i s e s s i n c e t h e n a n d t h e c o n t e n t i o n o f t h e CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors.

entities.text: Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Page No. 13 of 15 petitioners that the suit premises is lying locked since long is a false one.

Thus, the petitioners have miserably failed to prove that the respondents are using the tenanted premises for the purpose other than it was let out or that neither the respondents nor any of his family members are residing in the tenanted premises for a period of 6 months before filing the eviction petition.

The respondents on the other hand have clearly proved, by virtue of several documents, i.e., electricity bill, Income tax return, LIC premium receipt, photocopy of pass-book, Election ID card, that they are residing in the tenanted premises very much."

7.24. The same pleadings and the same evidence have come on record in the present case as no document could be produced by the plaintiff even in this case to prove that the tenanted premises was let out solely for residential purposes.

The rent receipts which have been produced by the plaintiff here, were also produced before the court of Rent Controller and it was rightly observed by the Rent Controller that the words 'Rehaishi' in the said rent receipts seem to have been added subsequently.

Even in the present case the court has gone through the said rent receipts Ex. PW 1/3 and PW 1/4 and it seems that the said word 'Rehaishi' in the said receipts has been added subsequently and even if not so, the same by itself does not prove that the property was let out solely Ved Prakash vs Vijay Laxmi on 2 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59662408/
8 for residential purposes.

It may be noted that in para 7 on page 6 of the plaint, it is mentioned that the tenanted premises is located in residential building and that the act of the defendants of storing tyres therein is not permissible under the By-Laws of MCD, however, no witness was examined by t h e p l a i n t i f f f r o m M C D t o p r o v e t h a t t h e b u i l d i n g i s r e s i d e n t i a l CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors.

entities.text: Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Page No. 14 of 15 and that the storing of tyres in the tenanted premises is not permissible under the By-Laws of the MCD.

It may be noted that in the cross examination of PW-4, PW-4 admitted that the plaintiff is also running a shop on the ground floor and that he is also storing goods on the upper floors of the property, from which an inference can be drawn that the property is not residential, as stated in the plaint and it is being used for storage of goods by the plaintiff as well as by the defendants.

Accordingly, no grounds are made to issue mandatory injunction so as to direct the defendants to remove his goods i.e. tyres etc. from the tenanted premises and so as to prohibit him from using the tenanted premises for providing accommodation to his servants and for cooking food therein.

7.26. 
Therefore, these issues are decided in favour of defendants and against the plaintiff.
8. FINAL ORDER
In view of finding of this court on the aforesaid issues, present suit is dismissed with cost.
9. However, copy of the order be sent to concerned Municipal Body, so that fire safety audit of the building be conducted to avoid any untoward incident.
10. Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
11. File be consigned to Record Room after necessary compliance.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Thus, even through cross examination of DW-1 Chetan  Gupta, the plaintiff could not prove the extent / nature / kind of  damage caused to the building or that any such damage was  caused due to storage of articles by the defendants and not  due to natural wear and tear, as the building is admittedly very  old.
These documents clearly prove that the tenanted premises is being used for residential purposes by the respondents and that the contention of the petitioner that none of the respondents is residing at the tenanted premises does not hold any ground.
On the other hand, the case of the respondents is that the said word "RIHAISH" has been added by the petitioners subsequently and that in the original rent receipts there is no said word "RIHAISH".
From perusal of the said rent receipts, it is clear that the said word has been added subsequently since it is not in proper column where it should have been stated.
No other document has been filed by the petitioners to show that the tenanted premises was let out solely for residential purposes.
The respondents have also filed copy of the electricity bill for the year 2011, 2012, 2013 and 2014 in order to prove that the respondents are residing in the t e n a n t e d p r e m i s e s s i n c e t h e n a n d t h e c o n t e n t i o n o f t h e CS No.13731/2016 Ved Prakash Vs. Vijay Laxmi & Ors.
Thus, the petitioners have miserably failed to prove that the respondents are using the tenanted premises for the purpose other than it was let out or that neither the respondents nor any of his family members are residing in the tenanted premises for a period of 6 months before filing the eviction petition.
The rent receipts which have been produced by the plaintiff here, were also produced before the court of Rent Controller and it was rightly observed by the Rent Controller that the words 'Rehaishi' in the said rent receipts seem to have been added subsequently.
Even in the present case the court has gone through the said rent receipts Ex. PW 1/3 and PW 1/4 and it seems that the said word 'Rehaishi' in the said receipts has been added subsequently and even if not so, the same by itself does not prove that the property was let out solely Ved Prakash vs Vijay Laxmi on 2 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59662408/
